'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Rod Grams]] | before_party = Republican Party (US) | after_election = [[Mark Dayton]] | after_party = Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party (Minnesota) }} {{Elections in Minnesota}} The '''2000 United States Senate election in Minnesota''' was held on November 7, 2000. Republican incumbent [[Rod Grams]] ran for a second consecutive term in office, but he was defeated by former [[Minnesota State Auditor|Minnesota state auditor]] [[Mark Dayton]]. Upon Dayton's swearing in, the Democratic Party held both of Minnesota's Senate seats for the first time since [[History of the Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party#Minnesota Massacre|1978]]. == DFL primary == *[[Mark Dayton]], former [[Minnesota State Auditor|Minnesota state auditor]] and nominee for Senate in [[1982 United States Senate election in Minnesota|1982]] *[[Michael V.
